2610.07638.title: Learning Explainable Representations of Complex Game-playing Strategies
2610.07638.paper_summary: As part of learning to play complex games, human players develop develop abstractions for concepts and strategies of gameplay consistent with game rules to improve their performance. These concepts are applied to explain other players' actions, and to inform their own actions in-game. Understanding other players' strategies is a crucial part of such improvement, but requires time and effort. In this paper, we propose a strategy similar to human cognition for training RL agents to synthesize learned strategies and policies as executable procedures based on sequences of gameplay actions. We present methods to automatically learn such programs to play chess and to solve tasks in a grid-based environment. We show that the learned strategies produce effective actions, and can be learned from gameplay data.
2610.07638.paper_summary_zh: 作為學習複雜遊戲的一部分，人類玩家發展出與遊戲規則一致的遊戲概念和策略的抽象，以提高他們的表現。這些概念被應用於解釋其他玩家的行動，並指導他們在遊戲中的行動。理解其他玩家的策略是這種改進的關鍵部分，但需要時間和努力。在本文中，我們提出了一種類似於人類認知的策略，用於訓練強化學習代理，將學習到的策略和政策合成為基於遊戲行動序列的可執行程序。我們提出了自動學習這些程序的方法，以便下棋和解決基於網格的環境中的任務。我們顯示學習到的策略能夠產生有效的行動，並且可以從遊戲數據中學習。
